1.title: Spiritual Blessings in Christ
1.themes: Election, Redemption, Sealed with the Holy Spirit, Paul's Prayer for Spiritual Wisdom
1.outline:
1. Greetings (1:1-2)
2. Spiritual Blessings (1:3-14)
3. Prayer for Revelation (1:15-23)
1.summary: Paul begins by praising God for the spiritual blessings given to believers in Christ, emphasizing predestination, redemption, and the sealing of the Holy Spirit. He concludes with a prayer for the Ephesians to have spiritual wisdom and to understand the great power of God demonstrated in Christ's resurrection.

2.title: Saved by Grace Through Faith
2.themes: Grace, Salvation, Unity of Jews and Gentiles in Christ
2.outline:
1. From Death to Life (2:1-10)
2. One in Christ (2:11-22)
2.summary: Paul explains that believers are saved by grace through faith, not by their own works, having been brought from spiritual death to life. He then illustrates how Christ has broken down the dividing wall of hostility between Jews and Gentiles, uniting them into one new humanity and a dwelling place for God.

3.title: The Mystery of the Gospel Revealed
3.themes: The Mystery of Christ, Paul's Ministry to the Gentiles, Prayer for Spiritual Strength
3.outline:
1. Paul's Ministry of the Mystery (3:1-13)
2. Prayer for Spiritual Empowerment (3:14-21)
3.summary: Paul describes his calling to preach the 'mystery' of Christ—that Gentiles are fellow heirs and members of the same body. He prays that the Ephesians may be strengthened by the Spirit and rooted in the immeasurable love of Christ, ending with a doxology praising God's power.

4.title: Unity and the New Life
4.themes: Unity in the Body of Christ, Spiritual Gifts, The Old vs. New Self
4.outline:
1. Unity in the Body (4:1-16)
2. Living as Children of Light (4:17-32)
4.summary: Paul urges believers to live worthy of their calling, maintaining the unity of the Spirit. He lists the spiritual gifts given to build up the church. He then contrasts their former way of life with the new life in Christ, instructing them to put away falsehood, anger, and bitterness, and instead be kind and forgiving.

5.title: Walking in Love and Light
5.themes: Imitating God, Light vs. Darkness, Spirit-Filled Living, Christian Marriage
5.outline:
1. Walk in Love (5:1-7)
2. Walk in Light (5:8-14)
3. Walk in Wisdom (5:15-21)
4. Instructions for Wives and Husbands (5:22-33)
5.summary: Believers are called to imitate God and walk in love, avoiding sexual immorality and impurity. They are to live as children of light, exposing darkness, and being filled with the Spirit. Paul then provides instructions on mutual submission, specifically detailing the roles of husbands and wives as a reflection of Christ and the church.

6.title: The Armor of God
6.themes: Children and Parents, Slaves and Masters, Spiritual Warfare, The Armor of God
6.outline:
1. Instructions for Children and Parents (6:1-4)
2. Instructions for Slaves and Masters (6:5-9)
3. The Armor of God (6:10-20)
4. Final Greetings (6:21-24)
6.summary: After addressing relationships between children and parents, and slaves and masters, Paul transitions to spiritual warfare. He commands believers to put on the full armor of God to stand firm against the devil's schemes. He concludes the letter with final greetings and a blessing of peace and grace.

1.title: To Live is Christ
1.themes: Thanksgiving, Joy in Suffering, Advancing the Gospel, To Live is Christ
1.outline:
1. Greetings and Prayer (1:1-11)
2. Paul's Imprisonment Advances the Gospel (1:12-18)
3. To Live is Christ, to Die is Gain (1:19-30)
1.summary: Paul expresses profound gratitude and joy for the Philippians' partnership in the gospel. He explains that his imprisonment has actually served to advance the gospel message. Torn between a desire to depart and be with Christ or remain in the flesh for their progress, he encourages them to live in a manner worthy of the gospel.

2.title: The Humility and Exaltation of Christ
2.themes: Humility, Christ's Example, Shining as Lights, Timothy and Epaphroditus
2.outline:
1. Imitating Christ's Humility (2:1-11)
2. Lights in the World (2:12-18)
3. Commendation of Timothy and Epaphroditus (2:19-30)
2.summary: Paul urges unity through humility, presenting the ultimate example: Jesus Christ, who emptied himself to become a servant and died on a cross, leading to His exaltation. Paul exhorts believers to work out their salvation and shine as lights. He also commends his co-workers, Timothy and Epaphroditus, for their faithful service.

3.title: Pressing Toward the Mark
3.themes: Righteousness Through Faith, Knowing Christ, Straining Toward the Goal, Heavenly Citizenship
3.outline:
1. Righteousness Through Faith (3:1-11)
2. Pressing on Toward the Goal (3:12-16)
3. Citizenship in Heaven (3:17-21)
3.summary: Warning against false teachers who rely on the flesh and the law, Paul counts all his previous accomplishments as loss compared to knowing Christ. He describes his pursuit of knowing Christ and the power of His resurrection, pressing on toward the heavenly prize. He reminds believers that their true citizenship is in heaven.

4.title: Rejoice in the Lord Always
4.themes: Joy, Peace, Right Thinking, Contentment, God's Provision
4.outline:
1. Exhortations to Unity and Joy (4:1-9)
2. Paul's Thanks for Their Gifts (4:10-20)
3. Final Greetings (4:21-23)
4.summary: Paul exhorts the Philippians to stand firm, resolve conflicts, and rejoice in the Lord always. He encourages them to bring their anxieties to God in prayer to experience His peace, and to focus their minds on whatever is true and good. He thanks them for their financial support, expressing his contentment in all circumstances through Christ's strength.

1.title: The Supremacy of Christ
1.themes: Thanksgiving, The Preeminence of Christ, Reconciliation, Paul's Labor for the Church
1.outline:
1. Greetings and Thanksgiving (1:1-14)
2. The Supremacy of the Son of God (1:15-23)
3. Paul's Labor for the Church (1:24-29)
1.summary: Paul gives thanks for the Colossians' faith and prays for their spiritual growth. He presents a powerful poem on the supremacy of Christ as the image of the invisible God, the creator, and the head of the church. He emphasizes that reconciliation comes through Christ's death and discusses his own suffering for the sake of presenting the mystery of Christ.

2.title: Fullness in Christ
2.themes: Spiritual Fullness, Freedom from Human Regulations, Warning Against False Philosophy
2.outline:
1. Alive in Christ (2:1-15)
2. Let No One Disqualify You (2:16-23)
2.summary: Paul expresses his struggle for the believers, desiring them to be rooted in Christ. He warns them against deceptive philosophies and human traditions. He asserts that in Christ they have been made full and alive, their sins forgiven and spiritual enemies disarmed, rendering legalistic rules and asceticism unnecessary and powerless.

3.title: Putting on the New Self
3.themes: Things Above, The Old vs. New Self, Rules for Christian Households
3.outline:
1. Put On the New Self (3:1-17)
2. Rules for Christian Households (3:18-25)
3.summary: Believers are instructed to set their minds on heavenly things, since they have been raised with Christ. They must put to death earthly desires and the practices of their old self, instead clothing themselves with compassion, kindness, humility, and love. Paul then provides practical household codes for wives, husbands, children, parents, and slaves.

4.title: Further Instructions and Greetings
4.themes: Prayer, Wisdom Toward Outsiders, Final Greetings
4.summary: Paul concludes his practical instructions by addressing masters, and then urges the church to devote themselves to prayer and to act wisely toward outsiders, letting their speech be gracious. He finishes the letter with a list of personal greetings from and to various co-workers, and a final request for them to remember his chains.
